title: Principle 6: Feedback: Don't dodge the punches
coreMove: Put imperfect work where correction can hit it while there is still time to adjust.
sourcePressure: Feedback means exposing work to useful correction instead of protecting errors because correction feels uncomfortable. The source sidecar contains no named people, studies, institutions, places, dates, or artifacts for this chapter, so named source anchors must be omitted rather than invented.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating all criticism as equally wise or turning feedback into generic praise and blame.

hook: Ch9: learner stares at browser tabs and realizes motivation is not enough
Ch9: broad modern world pressure opener
counterintuition: The obvious move is not the real move
Most people think more effort is enough
This is not about working harder

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: Claire, a grant writer sending an early draft while comments can still change it
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next month produces visible evidence or another private feeling of effort
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire sends the grant draft before polishing the language because the budget logic can still be corrected today.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a shared-document comment pane open beside a grant deadline calendar

exampleSpecs.domain: Chris, a design student hearing the same critique from two reviewers
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a deadline exposes the weakness early enough to adjust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chris writes down the design critique that two reviewers repeat and treats the repetition as data, not insult.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two critique sheets overlapping on a studio pinboard

exampleSpecs.domain: Antoine, a pottery seller posting imperfect product photos for real buyer response
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the learner keeps credibility with a reviewer, client, teacher, or team
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Antoine posts three imperfect pottery photos and watches which buyer question exposes the missing information.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a chipped mug photographed on a gray product backdrop

exampleSpecs.domain: Sofia, a lab assistant requesting comments tied to the grading standard
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the project survives contact with a real schedule and real standards
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sofia asks for lab comments only on the rubric dimension that will judge the assignment, not on general neatness.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a lab rubric folded beside a rack of labeled samples

exampleSpecs.domain: Chidi, a choir soloist recording a rough take for targeted correction
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether comfort keeps protecting the exact skill gap that matters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chidi records the rough choir solo and asks the conductor for one correction on breath timing.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a phone voice memo paused under a marked choral score

exampleSpecs.domain: Marta, a logistics planner filtering noisy comments without hiding from precise ones
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next attempt changes the skill instead of decorating the plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marta separates noisy logistics complaints from the one routing correction that keeps appearing in real deliveries.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a delivery map with three late stops marked in orange

skillTargets: seek correction while it can change the work
evaluate whether feedback matches the task standard
use discomfort without treating all criticism as useful

tryThisNowSpec: Send one unfinished piece of work to the smallest qualified reviewer and ask for one correction tied to the target standard.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
